terms.label: norm of a bounded linear transformation
proper vertex k-coloring of a simple graph

observations.text: Over real or complex normed vector spaces X,Y, a linear transformation T:X→Y belongs to the bounded-transformation space when there is one finite M>0 satisfying ||Tx||_Y≤M||x||_X for every x.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki Space of Bounded Linear Transformations uses a single uniform M; unlike its separate Bounded Linear Transformation page's invalid reversed-quantifier formulation.

observations.text: The norm of a bounded linear transformation is the supremum of the norms ||Tx|| over all input vectors with ||x|| at most one.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki Norm on Bounded Linear Transformation Definition 1; unit ball always contains zero.

observations.text: An equivalent norm is the infimum of positive constants C such that ||Tx||≤C||x|| holds for all x. For zero operator the infimum is zero.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki Definition 4; do not use its Definition 3 as printed for general codomain Y, where it writes ||Tx||_X rather than ||Tx||_Y.

observations.text: A proper k-vertex coloring of a simple graph assigns each vertex one of k labeled colors such that adjacent vertices have different colors; some palette colors need not occur.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki proper vertex coloring definition explicitly maps V→{1,…,k}; the map need not be surjective, and k≥1 under fixed positive-palette convention.

observations.text: A contraction mapping between metric spaces satisfies a global Lipschitz inequality with one constant 0≤q<1 for every pair of points of the domain.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki contraction of metric spaces; mapping need not map a space to itself and does not require domain completeness unless proving a fixed-point theorem.

meanings.context: Functional analysis: linear map X→Y between real or complex normed spaces with one global bound

formulations.text: Let X,Y be normed vector spaces over the same field F∈{ℝ,ℂ} and T:X→Y a linear map. T is bounded if there exists a real M≥0 such that ||Tx||_Y≤M||x||_X for every x∈X.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The uniform quantifier ∃M∀x is essential; ∀x∃M yields a condition automatically true for any linear map and is defective. A common scalar field and specified domain/codomain norms are retained.

meanings.display_term: norm of a bounded linear transformation
meanings.context: Functional analysis: operator norm on real/complex bounded linear maps between normed spaces

formulations.text: For a bounded linear T:X→Y between real or complex normed vector spaces, define ||T||=sup{||Tx||_Y : x∈X, ||x||_X≤1}. This is a finite nonnegative real number.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: Uses the source-backed supremum over the unit ball, including x=0. Boundedness ensures a finite supremum and allows X={0}, where ||T||=0.

formulations.text: For bounded linear T:X→Y between real or complex normed spaces, equivalently ||T||=inf{M>0 : ||Tx||_Y≤M||x||_X for all x∈X}, with infimum taken in [0,+∞].
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The alternative infimum-of-uniform-bounds formulation is equivalent to the unit-ball supremum; no illegal norm of Tx in X is used when T maps X into a different Y.

meanings.context: Graph theory: fixed integer k≥1, loopless simple undirected graph; coloring need not use every palette color

formulations.text: Let G=(V,E) be a loopless simple undirected graph and let k≥1 be an integer. A proper vertex k-coloring of G is a map c:V→{1,…,k} such that for every edge {u,v}∈E, c(u)≠c(v). Surjectivity is not required.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The source specifies a mapping to a palette with k labels and differing adjacent colors. This is separate from chromatic number (minimum k) and permits unused colors, including for an empty vertex set.

meanings.context: Metric spaces: globally Lipschitz mapping with a constant strictly below one

formulations.text: Let (X,d_X) and (Y,d_Y) be nonempty metric spaces and f:X→Y. The map f is a contraction if there exists q∈[0,1) such that d_Y(f(x),f(y))≤q·d_X(x,y) for all x,y∈X.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: Contraction is a pointwise global metric inequality, not a fixed-point theorem; no completeness or self-map is assumed. Domain and codomain metric spaces are nonempty to match the existing sourced metric-space meaning.

relations.editorial_reason: A bounded linear map requires two normed spaces with a shared real/complex scalar field and vector norms, grounded in the independently sourced normed-vector-space meaning.
The meaning relies on preserving vector addition and scalar multiplication, so the specific linear-transformation prerequisite should be sourced before screening the link.
relations.target_query: Linear transformation between two vector spaces over the same scalar field

relations.editorial_reason: A finite operator norm is defined here only for linear transformations satisfying the uniform bound; the newly sourced boundedness meaning supplies the exact restriction.
The infimum of admissible operator bounds is taken over all vectors and requires the same bounded linear transformation as the companion supremum formulation.
The condition on endpoints {u,v} relies on a loopless undirected simple graph, matching the independently reviewed simple graph context.
The contraction inequality uses domain and codomain metric distances; the existing reviewed metric-space meaning supplies both metric structures.

issues.reason: ProofWiki Definition:Bounded Linear Transformation (Normed Vector Space section) displays ∀v∃c>0 rather than the required ∃c>0∀v, which wrongly allows nonuniform bounds. The separately sourced bounded-transformation-space definition correctly uses a uniform M, so this draft follows that version.

ProofWiki Norm on Bounded Linear Transformation Definition 3 writes ||Ax||_X for general A:X→Y although Ax lies in Y; its Definitions 1,2,4 use the typed codomain correctly. The independent population adopts Definitions 1 and 4 and quarantines the inconsistent variant pending audit.
